errata.error: CPRA's export files CRMS0626's marsh well under the site's surface-water gauge, `CRMS0626-H01`, from 7 May 2009 to 2 June 2010: 8,721 rows whose `Sensor Environment` reads `Marsh Well`, 8,111 of them with an elevation. The marsh well measures water in the marsh soil.
errata.response: The adapter leaves out a surface-water gauge's elevations labeled `Marsh Well`, and fails on any other label but `Surface Water`, so no fetch brings these values. The ones the store already holds are flagged `suspect` over the span once `requalify` runs over it, since a refetch keeps the months it brings nothing for; a store backfilled anew doesn't hold them. Errata spans are whole days, so the two surface-water values of 2 June 2010, from 22:00 UTC, are flagged too.
errata.evidence: In CPRA's export of 8 November 2026, all 8,111 of those elevations equal the site's marsh well, `CRMS0626-W01`, at the same hour to the millimeter. The rows are `CRMS0626-H01`'s first, from 17:00 UTC on 7 May 2009. The well's own series ends at 21:00 UTC on 2 June 2010, and `CRMS0626-H01`'s surface-water rows start at 22:00. No other `H0n` series in the export has a row that isn't `Surface Water`. GESLA's CRMS0626 record isn't the well: it matches `CRMS0626-W01` on 1 to 7% of hours a year.
